facts.statement: Nuthetes is a coelurosaurian theropod dinosaur that is classified as either a dromaeosaurid or a tyrannosauroid.
facts.quote: Nuthetes is a genus of coelurosaurian theropod dinosaur, either a dromaeosaurid or tyrannosauroid

facts.statement: The genus name Nuthetes means "one who admonishes" or "a monitor," referencing the similarity of its teeth to modern monitor lizards.
facts.quote: The generic name Nuthetes is derived from the Koine Greek nouthetes, a contraction of νουθέτητης (nouthetetes) meaning "one who admonishes" or "a monitor," in reference to the similarity of Nuthetes teeth to those of a modern monitor lizard

facts.statement: The species name destructor means "destroyer," referring to teeth adapted for piercing and cutting prey in an animal estimated to be the size of a Bengal monitor.
facts.quote: The specific name is Latin for "destroyer", a reference to "the adaptations of the teeth for piercing, cutting, and lacerating the prey" of a form he estimated to be equal in size to the present Bengal monitor

facts.statement: Nuthetes destructor was named and described by Richard Owen in 1854.
facts.quote: N. destructor was named and described by Richard Owen in 1854

facts.statement: The holotype was collected by amateur paleontologist Charles Willcox from the Feather Quarry near Durlston Bay.
facts.quote: The holotype, DORCM G 913, was collected by Charles Willcox, an amateur paleontologist living at Swanage, from the Feather Quarry near Durlston Bay

facts.statement: The holotype was thought to be lost until it was rediscovered in the 1970s at the Dorset County Museum.
facts.quote: The holotype was once thought to be lost but was rediscovered during the 1970s in the Dorset County Museum

facts.statement: Fossils of Nuthetes have been found in the Early Cretaceous (middle Berriasian) Lulworth Formation in England and the Angeac-Charente bonebed in France.
facts.quote: found in rocks of the middle Berriasian age (Early Cretaceous) in the Cherty Freshwater Member of the Lulworth Formation in England and also the Angeac-Charente bonebed in France

facts.statement: Richard Owen originally classified Nuthetes as a lizard and later as a crocodilian.
facts.quote: Nuthetes was originally classified by Owen as a lizard and a varanid; later he changed his mind concluding it was a crocodilian

facts.statement: Richard Lydekker was the first to correctly identify Nuthetes as a dinosaur in 1888.
facts.quote: Only in 1888 Richard Lydekker did understand it was a dinosaur

facts.statement: A 2002 re-examination by Angela Milner suggested Nuthetes most likely belonged to a subadult dromaeosaurid.
facts.quote: In 2002 however, a re-examination of the fossils by paleontologist Angela Milner showed that they most likely belonged to a subadult dromaeosaurid

facts.statement: Steve Sweetman concluded that Nuthetes destructor is a velociraptorine dromaeosaurid based on an examination of five fossil teeth specimens.
facts.quote: Steve Sweetman examined five good specimens of fossil teeth and confirmed that they belong to Nuthetes destructor, and concluded that this species is a velociraptorine dromaeosaurid

facts.statement: Researchers Rauhut, Milner, and Moore-Fay (2010) noted the similarity between Nuthetes teeth and those of the basal tyrannosauroid Proceratosaurus, suggesting caution in classifying isolated teeth as dromaeosaurids.
facts.quote: Rauhut, Milner and Moore-Fay (2010) pointed out the great similarity of the teeth of basal tyrannosauroid Proceratosaurus to the teeth of velociraptorine dromaeosaurids

facts.statement: Fossils once attributed to Nuthetes were later identified in 2002 as osteoderms from a turtle, not the dinosaur.
facts.quote: Owen in 1878 also assumed some fossilised scutes, of a type for which he coined the name "granicones", belonged to Nuthetes but these were in 2002 shown to be limb or tail osteoderms of a turtle

facts.statement: If Nuthetes was a dromaeosaurid, it would have been a small predator.
facts.quote: If it was a dromaeosaurid, Nuthetes would have been a small predator

facts.statement: Nuthetes lived between 143.1 and 137.05 million years ago during the Berriasian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Berriasian to Berriasian (143.1 to 137.05 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Nuthetes is known only from fossil teeth and jaw fragments.
rejected.quote: known only from fossil teeth and jaw fragments
